# Runtime compatibility probes

`workflows/runtime-certification/probes.json` is the stack-neutral probe contract.
The control plane snapshots this source revision with the actual sandbox, native
binary, worker, mounts, environment, authority and hooks before requesting probes.
It substitutes only the operator-selected existing protected canary path. Run these
bounded instructions only in disposable verification workspaces.

Each named phase is separately admitted, approved when required, and accounted for.
The interrupt phase is expected to end with signal status 143 after the controller
observes the requested sleep in its exact process group for at least 35 seconds.
Recovery uses the captured thread and cumulative-usage baseline. Six usage phases
separate ordinary turns, explicit compaction, model change and reconnect behavior;
compaction is paid work subject to the same admission as a model turn.

Passing requires actual protected-path hook refusal, schema-valid output, unchanged
tracked and untracked target contents, read-only mount refusal when applicable,
detached running evidence, same-thread recovery, and measured compaction/counter
semantics. A model's assertion of success, accepted configuration flags, an absent
usage field, or a stale report cannot substitute for an observation.

The controller captures the runtime stream directly into host-only evidence, embeds
trusted worker/request bytes in its launch, and preserves raw observations in its
hashed attestation. Concurrent application writers must be excluded from the sandbox
during certification. Compatibility evidence does not authorize a policy change,
credential capability, application launch, or deployment by itself.

The real acceptance exercise must additionally kill/restart the controller and prove
that its detached execution survives, that ambiguous paid launches are observed
rather than retried, and that altered evidence or a recreated identity refuses use.
